title: JOINs
objective: A join combines related entities through their key relationships. The join cardinality determines whether rows disappear or multiply.
misconception: The starter joins the project to a user with the same numeric ID, not its owner_id; it also has no tenant scope.
acceptance: A JOIN on similarly named IDs is not evidence of a relationship. Read the foreign-key declaration and choose INNER JOIN versus LEFT JOIN intentionally. A database key alone does not enforce row-level authorization.
securityBoundary: Incorrect ON predicates can silently return no rows—or connect a record to the wrong person.
